admin.mail.providers.title: SMTP providers
admin.mail.providers.description: Platform email goes through the first enabled provider by priority. When its daily limit is used up or it returns an error (authentication, quota, outage), the next one takes the message. Events without their own SMTP use the same list.
admin.mail.providers.empty: No providers yet. Add the first one so the platform can send email.
admin.mail.providers.envActive: No provider is enabled, so email goes through SMTP_* from the environment. Enable or add a provider and it replaces it.
admin.mail.providers.orderHint: The provider with the lower number is tried first. The daily limit is counted in UTC and restarts at UTC midnight.
admin.mail.providers.deleteBody: Email will no longer go through it. The saved password is lost.
admin.mail.providers.dialogDescription: The SMTP server the platform sends email through.
admin.mail.providers.name: Name
admin.mail.providers.dailyLimitHelp: How many emails per day this provider allows. Counted in UTC. When the limit is used up the next provider takes the message; with no other provider the message is deferred and sent later. Empty means no limit.
admin.mail.providers.senderHelp: Empty fields use the platform sender. The address must be verified at this provider. Event email is always sent as the Event.
admin.agents.title: Agents
admin.agents.subtitle: The clusters where the platform runs laboratories: connection, priority, capacity and certificates.
admin.agents.empty: No agents yet. Add the first one to run laboratories.
admin.agents.error.name: Enter the agent name, up to {max} characters.
admin.agents.error.endpoint: The address must be host:port, with no scheme or path.
admin.agents.error.priority: Priority must be a whole number from 0 to {max}.
admin.agents.feature.unknown: The agent has not reported its features yet
admin.agents.form.name: Name
admin.agents.form.endpointHelp: The agent host and port, for example agent.example.com:443. No scheme or path. The address cannot be changed after adding.
admin.agents.form.tokenHelp: The one-time token the cluster administrator gave. The platform does not store it and never shows it again.
admin.agents.form.priorityHelp: A smaller number is chosen first. Equal priorities are ordered by name.
admin.agents.form.caHelp: Only for clusters with a self-signed certificate (development stands). Paste the PEM.
admin.agents.form.caKeepHelp: Leave empty to keep the current CA certificate.
admin.agents.add.title: Add agent
admin.agents.add.description: The platform enrolls in the cluster with the one-time token and generates all keys itself.
admin.agents.edit.title: Agent “{name}”
admin.agents.edit.description: Name and priority. The address, certificate and keys do not change.
admin.agents.reconnect.title: Reconnect agent “{name}”?
admin.agents.reconnect.description: The same cluster is enrolled again with a new token and new keys. The record, priority and laboratories stay.
admin.agents.renew.title: Renew the certificate of agent “{name}”?
admin.agents.renew.body: The platform gets a new certificate for a new key. It is also renewed automatically 10 days before it ends.
admin.agents.renew.done: The certificate of agent “{name}” was renewed.
admin.agents.rotate.title: Replace the access key of agent “{name}”?
admin.agents.rotate.body: New laboratory links are signed with the new key. The old key keeps working for 15 more minutes and is then removed.
admin.agents.rotate.done: The access key of agent “{name}” was replaced.
admin.agents.delete.title: Delete agent “{name}”?
admin.agents.delete.body: Its keys, certificate and address are wiped; the record stays in the history. The cluster can be added again with a new enrollment.
admin.agents.delete.reservations: These future reservations lose capacity and become not covered ({count}):
admin.agents.delete.blockedBody: The agent still holds laboratories ({count}). Switch it off, wait for them to finish, then delete it.
admin.agents.clearCa.title: Remove the CA certificate of agent “{name}”?
admin.agents.clearCa.body: The platform stops trusting the self-signed server certificate. If the cluster uses one, the connection will not recover until the CA is set again by reconnecting.
admin.agents.clearCa.done: The CA certificate of agent “{name}” was removed.
